title: My God, Consider My Distress
description: My God, Consider My Distress in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 12, headed “Breathing after comfort and deliverance”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, con-sid-er my dis-tress, Let mer-cy plead my cause; Tho' I have sinn'd a-gainst thy grace, I can't for-get thy laws.

lines: Tho' I have sinn'd against thy grace,
Uphold my life, uphold my hopes,
Be thou a surety, Lord, for me,
But make thy waiting servant see
"When will the Lord his truth fulfil,
Look down upon my sorrows, Lord,
And shew thy grace the same
As thou art ever wont t' afford
To those that love thy Name.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
